title: What happens when you type a URL (and press Enter)
description:
Before a page appears, your browser does four jobs in a row. Byte and Compy walk through them.

#networking #webdev #programming #shorts
angle: Typing a URL triggers a fixed chain: DNS lookup, TCP connection, TLS handshake, then the HTTP request, and each step must finish before the next.
hook: You press Enter on a URL. What actually happens in the half second before the page shows up?

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: You press Enter on a URL. What actually happens before the page shows up?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Four steps, in order. Name lookup, connection, encryption, then the actual request.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Step one. The browser only knows the name. Computers need a number.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: DNS is the phone book. The name goes in, an IP address comes out.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Then it knocks on that address. Port 443 for secure sites.

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: First a short handshake to connect, then another to check the certificate and encrypt.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Only now does it ask for the page?

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Yes. The server answers with a status code and the page. Each step waits for the one before.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: And the browser repeats this for every image and script?

props.sub: requests per page, give or take

scenes.speaker: compy
scenes.narration: Same chain, many times. Which is why a slow DNS lookup makes everything feel slow.

scenes.speaker: byte
scenes.narration: Follow for more. Next: null, the billion dollar mistake.

claims.text: Loading a page follows the order: parse URL, DNS lookup, TCP connection (port 443 for https), TLS handshake, HTTP request, response, render
